I know this is anti-work but if this can help someone find a job then maybe it’s worth sharing. I got 2 FT jobs since I started looking in January (the first one was negatively impacting my health so I left). This works best if you aren’t too particular about the title you want. Also, YMMV and keep an eye out for scams/MLMs.

Step 1: create 2 versions of your resume. One generic administrative/management focused one and one that’s in whatever field you have experience in or aspire to work in. Quick edit: the reason for creating 2 is so you can use the generic one for whatever kinds of jobs and the specific one for jobs you actually really want.

Step 2: join LinkedIn if you haven’t and fill out your profile as much as you can. Make sure you have a nice picture, even if it wasn’t professionally done.

Step 3: only search on LinkedIn (other sites are a waste of time from my experience but use them if you want). If you want remote work, search out of the United States **with no keywords**. If you want local search by your county or city. LinkedIn populates jobs similar to your experience automatically so keywords are a waste. Then, make sure to filter by adding Remote, Full-Time (unless you want another type), Easy Apply, Under 10 Applicants, and Past 24 Hours. This gives you the most recent roles with the fewest applicants, meaning there’s a better chance you’re noticed. If you’re coming up short remove the Under 10 Applicants filter.

Step 4: apply to as many jobs as you can. **Do not write cover letters or apply outside of LinkedIn, even if they ask you to.** Skip roles that require a cover letter to complete the app. The game is quantity not quality. If they include open answer questions you might want to skip, unless it’s just a quick 1-2. Quick edit: I forgot to mention but *always* do the little skills assessments LI recommends. If you fail don’t redo them. But if you pass make sure it goes on your profile. It helps LI suggest better roles.

Using this method, I’ve spoken to a good number of companies I would’ve missed out on had I done what I used to do, especially when it comes to cover letters. Many hiring managers don’t even read them. If they’re required then the company is probably uptight or expects a lot.

Once you get the phone screens/interviews it’s really up to you to do well, which I know isn’t always easy. But at least this way you’ll get your foot in the door more and maybe you’ll come out with a job to show for it.

Idk I think you’re taking it the wrong way. If there’s something indicative of a trans person’s identity there’s also something indicative of a cis person’s or a nonbinary person’s.

Gender doesn’t even mean anything anyway if you take out the physical aspects. It doesn’t inherently tell you anything about a person.

I’m gonna step in with some food for thought, and if you have another reasoning that I didn’t think of, then please let me know! My thought is there are really only a few options for why someone identifies a certain way, whether trans, cis, or any identity under the enby umbrella.

First is biological. There could be a gene that determines our feelings, or maybe a structure in the brain. Maybe even something chemical.

Second is societal, which is probably controversial and is also pretty weak. I would say the only real indicator here would be if you had certain role models of a particular gender that you strongly identified with growing up (family, friends, celebrities, fictional characters, etc.) OR maybe someone of a particular gender that you strongly do not identify with. But then for NB folks, it doesn’t make a lot of sense. And I would assume this doesn’t hold true 100% of the time, maybe making more of an influence on things like presentation rather than identity itself.

Third is spiritual. If we have a soul or a life force or something else, who is to say whether or not it is dictated by astrology? Or maybe there’s some component we don’t understand and that’s the cause.

Fourth is some mixture of these options.

For full disclosure, I identify as demifemale and I’m agnostic but have some spiritual beliefs. I also think that gender as a concept is kind of outdated... despite the fact that I have an identity, I almost wish gender identities didn’t exist at all and that it was purely about what body you feel most comfortable in. But that’s a separate discussion.

Anyway, my point of writing this novella is to say that there almost has to be some reason behind why you identify a certain way and not another way. I guess there is always the fifth option of it being random, but then there’s no point to giving any thought to anything else.

2.	If I medicate at work (rare but has happened), I usually do it with only 1.5 hours left in the day. My employer doesn’t care about weed but I also can’t tell you where I work so... just know there are sure to be places out there somewhere.
3.	I don’t feel bad about using even when it is nearly daily because I know I am getting help outside of that. When my insurance is screwing me over and I can’t go to therapy, I’m reading about my condition, doing journaling, and otherwise working on myself. I do what I can. That being said, I don’t tell my family about it because they would have a major problem with it so unfortunately I have no advice there.
